That the Court has not always covered itself in glory while guarding the house we live in is, in its own words, a shame that deserves to be buried ten fathoms deep . Amidst reluctant whispers of the 'E' word (Emergency Lite, if you will) today, its ears surely must prick up. items.title: Ten years without Najeeb: What happened to the ‘Idea of JNU’ and its promise of equality?
items.summary: On October 15, 2016, Najeeb Ahmed, a student at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), went missing. The disappearance came a day after an alleged altercation with members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). In the days that followed, students demanded answers from the university administration and sought accountability for what had happened. A movement emerged around a question that should never have become so difficult to ask: Where is Najeeb? Ten years later, that question remains unanswered. The official investigation was closed after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed its closure report, which a Delhi court accepted in June 2025. The Delhi High Court subsequently upheld the decision in December 2025 . The courts have not established what happened to Najeeb or where he is. But Najeeb's disappearance raises another question, one that concerns the political life of the university itself: whatever happened to the “Idea of JNU”?
